incidents.victim: TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenAI, and ~400 other npm/PyPI packages
incidents.vector: Compromised maintainer accounts pushed the self-propagating Shai-Hulud worm into TanStack's npm packages, which then republished malware into hundreds of dependent libraries to harvest developer credentials, cloud tokens, and code-signing keys.
incidents.impact: OpenAI confirmed two employee devices were impacted, with limited credential exfiltration from a small set of source code repositories, and is rotating macOS signing certificates by June 12. Mistral AI confirmed temporary access to non-core code repositories, and the attackers leaked or offered stolen source code from Mistral for sale on May 13. TeamPCP publicly released the Shai-Hulud worm source code on May 14-15, raising the risk of further attacks.

incidents.victim: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry) North American factories
incidents.vector: Nitrogen ransomware group, which historically uses SEO poisoning and trojanized installers (Advanced IP Scanner, AnyDesk, WinSCP, Cisco AnyConnect) for initial access, struck multiple Foxconn North American facilities.
incidents.impact: Production was disrupted at several Foxconn factories before being restored. Nitrogen claims to have exfiltrated 8TB of data (~11 million files), including confidential schematics, motherboard/PCB diagrams, thermal-design specs, and manufacturing process documents referencing Apple, Intel, Google, Nvidia, AMD, Dell, HPE, JPMorgan, Renesas, ASPEED, and Tencent.

incidents.victim: European/Central Asian government, diplomatic, and Ukrainian targets
incidents.vector: The Kazuar malware family — operated by a Russian FSB-linked actor Microsoft tracks under a 'Blizzard' codename — has evolved into a modular peer-to-peer botnet using Pelmeni droppers, .NET loaders, COM objects, and three module types (Kernel, Bridge, Worker) with EWS, HTTPS, and WebSocket fallback channels.
incidents.impact: The architecture supports stealthy long-term access for intelligence collection across government and diplomatic targets in Europe and Central Asia, plus systems in Ukraine previously compromised by a separate Russian GRU-linked actor. The actor staggers exfiltration to working hours and elects a single 'leader' module per botnet to reduce visible C2 traffic.

incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager customers
incidents.vector: Cisco Talos confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, an authentication-bypass flaw in Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager (vSmart/vManage). Talos tracks the campaign as UAT-8616, a sophisticated actor previously seen exploiting CVE-2026-20127 in the same products and using Operational Relay Box (ORB) infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Post-exploitation behavior includes adding SSH keys, modifying NETCONF configurations, and escalating to root. Talos also observed widespread, separate exploitation of CVE-2026-20133, CVE-2026-20128, and CVE-2026-20122 since March using public ZeroZenX Labs PoC code that deploys XenShell, Godzilla, Behinder, AdaptixC2, Sliver, XMRig, and a Nim-based 'agent1' implant.

incidents.vector: Lapsus$ obtained Vodafone source code through unspecified intrusion and used it as extortion leverage.
incidents.impact: Lapsus$ leaked portions of Vodafone source code after the company refused to pay the ransom demand.

incidents.vector: Attackers maintained unauthorized access to Best Western's reservation systems for over six months between October 2025 and April 2026; the initial vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Guest reservation data across Best Western, Sure Hotels, and WorldHotels brands was accessible to the intruder for the duration of the breach; the chain is now notifying affected guests.

incidents.vector: A China-linked espionage group (FamousSparrow) targeted an unpatched Microsoft Exchange server, then used a two-stage DLL sideloading technique that conditioned its payload on a specific execution path to evade sandbox analysis. The Deed RAT remote-access tool was installed.
incidents.impact: Bitdefender observed three intrusions between late December 2025 and end of February 2026 against the same victim. IT workstations were affected but the operational technology (OT) network was not. The intrusion represents China's first observed targeting of Azerbaijani industry, expanding cyber-espionage into Russia's traditional South Caucasus sphere of influence.

incidents.victim: Mexican government agencies (six entities) and Brazilian financial-services firms
incidents.vector: Trend Micro disclosed two AI-driven 'vibe-hacking' campaigns: Shadow-Aether-040 (Spanish-speaking) and Shadow-Aether-064 (Brazilian Portuguese). The actors jailbroke Anthropic's Claude via an agentic CLI claiming 'authorized red-team' work, then directed the AI to use Shodan/VulDB for vulnerability discovery, deploy web shells, generate custom backdoors (Python 'implante_http'), and dynamically generate scanning, password-spraying, and exploitation scripts.
incidents.impact: Six Mexican government entities were compromised between Dec 27 and Jan 4, with data theft in some cases. Shadow-Aether-064 has been targeting Brazilian financial organizations since April to steal financial data. Custom AI-generated tools evaded signature-based detection in most cases.

incidents.vector: A rogue version of the official Checkmarx Jenkins Application Security Testing (AST) plugin was published on the Jenkins Marketplace and contained an infostealer.
incidents.impact: Developers and CI/CD environments that installed the compromised plugin had credentials and secrets exposed to attackers; the vendor warned users to roll back and rotate credentials.

incidents.victim: Hugging Face users downloading fake 'OpenAI Privacy Filter' model
incidents.vector: A malicious repository impersonating OpenAI's Privacy Filter open-weight model briefly reached the #1 trending position on Hugging Face. It delivered a Rust-based information stealer to Windows users.
incidents.impact: The malicious repository drew approximately 244,000 downloads before being identified, exposing affected Windows users to credential theft via the embedded stealer.

incidents.vector: 126 malicious Google Chrome extensions (cluster tracked as 'WaSteal') posed as WhatsApp business helpers and intercepted WhatsApp web content, including messages, session cookies, and audio.
incidents.impact: Approximately 146,000 installations of the malicious extensions were observed, predominantly targeting Brazilian users. Stolen data enables account takeover and downstream financial fraud.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited an unspecified vulnerability in Skoda's German web store to access customer data.
incidents.impact: Skoda confirmed that customer data was likely accessed during the breach of its Germany online store; scope and victim count have not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: A ransomware actor (unnamed) struck West Pharmaceutical Services in early May, impacting global business operations.
incidents.impact: Per West's SEC filing, the attack disrupted manufacturing, shipping, and receiving operations globally. Some locations have restored operations, but the incident is material enough to require public disclosure and affected a major supplier of pharmaceutical drug packaging.

incidents.vector: Attackers published hundreds of malicious Ruby gems on May 11-12 containing code aimed at RubyGems staff. The gems attempted cross-site scripting against the registry and data theft from engineers' systems.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups in response and pulled the malicious packages. Details of what data the attackers were targeting from staff systems remain unclear. Incident is unrelated to the contemporaneous TanStack/Shai-Hulud npm campaign.

incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas LMS — 275M students and faculty across ~9,000 institutions
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited an issue in Instructure's 'Free-for-Teacher' account functionality (the same flaw as an earlier breach) to access user data. On May 7, the group defaced the Canvas login page with a ransom note after Instructure's initial 'containment' claim, prompting the platform to be pulled offline mid-exam season.
incidents.impact: Stolen data includes names, email addresses, student IDs, and messages between users at affected institutions. Instructure ultimately paid the ransom on May 11 in exchange for digital confirmation of data destruction. The House Homeland Security Committee has summoned Instructure leadership for a hearing.

incidents.vector: CISA added CVE-2026-6973, an improper input validation vulnerability in Ivanti EPMM, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog based on evidence of active in-the-wild exploitation.
incidents.impact: Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must remediate by CISA's deadline; the vulnerability is being actively exploited and represents the latest in a recurring pattern of Ivanti EPMM zero-days under attack.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS customers (PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls)
incidents.vector: Likely state-sponsored cluster CL-STA-1132 exploited zero-day CVE-2026-0300, a buffer overflow in PAN-OS Captive Portal (User-ID Authentication Portal), to inject shellcode into an nginx worker and gain unauthenticated root RCE. Exploitation attempts began April 9; successful RCE was achieved a week later.
incidents.impact: Attackers deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools, conducted Active Directory enumeration using credentials harvested from firewall service accounts, and systematically destroyed nginx crash logs, ptrace audit records, and core dumps. A SAML flood on April 29 was used to fail over to a second device, which was then also compromised.

incidents.victim: TAC cross-chain platform and Transit Finance cross-chain aggregator
incidents.vector: Both heists targeted legacy smart contracts interacting with the TON blockchain on the same day. Attackers exploited a four-year-old legacy contract on Transit Finance, and a similar contract pattern on TAC.
incidents.impact: Transit Finance lost approximately $1.9 million; TAC lost approximately $2.8 million. Transit Finance pledged to compensate affected users.

incidents.victim: Australian organizations running cPanel/WHM hosting control panel
incidents.vector: ASD's ACSC issued a critical alert for active exploitation of CVE-2026-41940, an authentication-bypass flaw in cPanel/WHM that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to reach the control panel and achieve remote code execution. The vulnerability affects all versions after 11.40 (2013); patches were released on April 30.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation observed in Australia; no specific industry or sector is being preferentially targeted, but the install base is extremely large given the age range of vulnerable versions. Unpatched, internet-exposed control panels are at acute risk.

incidents.vector: A 23-year-old train enthusiast in Taiwan used a software-defined radio and online-purchased hardware to spoof a TETRA-protocol General Alarm message to the THSR operations center.
incidents.impact: THSR ordered emergency braking on three high-speed bullet trains in the area of the spoofed signal, causing a 48-minute service disruption and triggering an anti-terrorism response. The incident underscores systemic weakness in unauthenticated emergency radio protocols still used by rail operators globally; new reporting May 15.

incidents.vector: A DPRK-nexus actor distributed trojanized software via a supply-chain compromise targeting a cryptocurrency platform. CrowdStrike's 2026 Financial Services Threat Landscape Report (released May 14) catalogs this as the single largest financial theft ever reported.
incidents.impact: $1.46 billion in cryptocurrency stolen — the largest single financial theft on record. Part of $2.02 billion total DPRK-nexus digital-asset theft in 2025 (a 51% year-over-year increase), with proceeds directly funding the regime's military programs.

incidents.vector: An attacker maintained root access to infrastructure at Huge Networks — a Brazilian DDoS-protection ISP — and used it to mass-scan the internet for insecure routers (e.g., TP-Link Archer AX21) and misconfigured open DNS resolvers to build a powerful DNS amplification/reflection botnet.
incidents.impact: The botnet has powered an extended campaign of massive DDoS attacks against other Brazilian network operators. Huge Networks' CEO told KrebsOnSecurity the activity stemmed from a security breach of his company, possibly by a competitor seeking to tarnish its reputation.
